title: Policy Documents — library, upload, versions and Test a question
story: The Policy Assistant answers only from documents that Graduate School staff keep in a library. This case shows that library: the two built-in official sources (the Graduate School Handbook 2022-2023 and the Research Protocol AY 2024-2025), the Operations Manual, which is held as a Draft until the Graduate School validates it, and how staff add a new policy document, replace it with a new version and check that the assistant finds it.

The demonstration document is made up for the walkthrough: a one-page memo with a lounge reservation rule. It is created with a time stamp in its title so a re-run does not collide, and it is removed at the end. No official document is changed or deleted.
accounts: Policy Documents is a staff and administrator screen only
data: Walkthrough Memo - Lounge Reservation <date-time stamp>, for example 20261001-0750
Lounge_Reservation_Memo_<stamp>.pdf (one page): a student organisation may reserve the Graduate School lounge at most four (4) times per semester
Lounge_Reservation_Memo_<stamp>_v2.pdf: the same memo with six (6) times
First upload for the walkthrough; then: Raised the limit from four to six reservations
Can a student withdraw a subject on Day 1?  |  How many times may a student organisation reserve the Graduate School lounge per semester?

parts.title: Part A - The library and the Draft Operations Manual

steps.text: Sign in as **staff@usls.edu.ph** and open **Policy Documents** under Monitoring & support. The page is titled **Policy document library**. Four counters show the number of sources, staff uploads, drafts pending validation and sources ready for the assistant. Below them are the **Test a question** panel and the **Documents** list with a search box and category and status filters.

shots.caption: The Policy document library: counters, Test a question, and the document cards.

steps: Read the three starting cards. The **Graduate School Handbook 2022-2023** (PDF, Handbook) and the **Graduate School Research Protocol (AY 2024-2025)** (DOCX, Research Protocol) are built-in sources: they are view-only. Every card shows its category, version, file type, size, and the number of searchable sections, and the **Actions** menu (three dots) offers View document and, for staff uploads, Edit details, Replace file and Remove.

steps.text: Type **Operations Manual** in the search box. The card for **USLS Graduate School Operations Manual (draft for validation)** has the amber status **Draft** and an amber warning: Draft - pending Graduate School validation. Assistant answers that use this document say so. Its note reads Prepared by the capstone group for Graduate School validation. Open **Version history** on the card to see version 1, marked Current, searched.

shots.caption: The Operations Manual is a Draft: it is searched, but every answer that uses it is flagged as pending validation.

steps.text: In **Test a question**, type **Can a student withdraw a subject on Day 1?** and select **Find passages**. The panel reports the passages found by keyword search, then an **Answer preview** extracted from the passages with no AI. The first passage is the Operations Manual, section 4.4 Withdrawal of subject, with the status Draft: Day 1 is inside the first week, so a student may withdraw a subject on Day 1 with the Dean's approval, but it is not free: 10% of the term's total due in the first week and 20% in the second. The preview ends with the line Draft - pending Graduate School validation. Further passages cite the Handbook (p. 53) and other sections of the manual.

shots.caption: Test a question on the Day 1 case: the cited source is the Draft Operations Manual, section 4.4, flagged as pending validation.

parts.title: Part B - Upload a new policy document

steps.text: Select **Add document**. The **Add policy document** dialog opens: a drop area for a PDF or DOCX file (up to 20 MB), then Document title, Category, Effective date, Status (Active, Draft or Archived), Description and Version note.

shots.caption: The Add policy document dialog, empty.

steps.text: Choose the file **Lounge_Reservation_Memo_<stamp>.pdf**, enter the title **Walkthrough Memo - Lounge Reservation <stamp>**, set Category to **Memo**, leave Status on Active, add the description and the version note **First upload for the walkthrough**.

shots.caption: The dialog filled with the file, title, category, description and version note.

steps.text: Select **Upload and index**. The file is read and indexed, the dialog closes and a green notice reads: the document was added to the Policy Assistant library. The counters change to 4 sources and 2 staff uploads.

shots.caption: Upload complete: the notice confirms the document is in the Policy Assistant library.

steps.text: Search the list for the time stamp. The card shows Category Memo, Version 1, type PDF, 1 page, 1 searchable section, who uploaded it and when.

shots.caption: The new card: one page, one searchable section, uploaded by Grace Fernandez.

parts.title: Part C - Test a question, then replace the file

steps.text: Clear the search, type **How many times may a student organisation reserve the Graduate School lounge per semester?** in Test a question and select **Find passages**. The panel reports 1 passage found. The Answer preview reads According to Walkthrough Memo - Lounge Reservation <stamp>, p. 1: a student organisation may reserve the Graduate School lounge at most four (4) times per semester. The passage card names the document, status Active, and the page, p. 1. A policy uploaded a minute ago is already searchable.

shots.caption: Test a question: the new memo is found, with its document name and page.

steps.text: On the new card, open the **Actions** menu and choose **Replace file**. The **Replace file** dialog says the new file becomes version 2 and that the current one stays in the version history and is no longer searched. Choose **Lounge_Reservation_Memo_<stamp>_v2.pdf** and enter **Raised the limit from four to six reservations** under What changed.

shots.caption: Replace file: the dialog explains that the old version is kept but no longer searched.

steps.text: Select **Replace and re-index**. The notice reads that the file was replaced and re-indexed and that the previous version is kept in the version history. The Test a question panel still shows the earlier answer, because it is not re-run by itself.

shots.caption: After the replacement: the notice, with the earlier test result still on screen.

steps.text: Open **Version history (2)** on the card. Version 2 is marked **Current, searched** with its note; Version 1 is listed below it with its own file name and note, each with a **View** link.

shots.caption: Version history: version 2 is the current, searched version; version 1 is kept for the record.

steps.text: Run the same question again. The Answer preview now reads six (6) times per semester. The assistant uses only the current version.

shots.caption: The same question after the replacement: the answer follows version 2.

parts.title: Part D - Clean up what was created

steps.text: Open the **Actions** menu on the walkthrough memo and choose **Remove**. A confirmation asks Remove this policy document? and explains that the document and all stored versions are deleted and the Policy Assistant stops using them, and that setting the status to Archived keeps the record without searching it.

shots.caption: The confirmation before a staff upload is removed.

steps.text: Select **Remove document**. A notice confirms the removal and the counters return to 3 sources and 1 staff upload (the Draft Operations Manual). The Remove action exists only on staff uploads; the built-in sources cannot be removed.

shots.caption: The memo is removed; the official documents are untouched.

notes: The Operations Manual is a Draft pending Graduate School validation. It is searched, and any answer that uses it says it is a draft. The Handbook and the Research Protocol are the official sources.
Test a question shows the passages the assistant would use and an extracted preview without AI; it is a retrieval check, not the assistant's final wording (see {case:policy-assistant}).
Only PDF and DOCX files are accepted; scanned PDFs are read with OCR when it is installed. Upload and replace each rebuild the search index for that document.

The memo used here is made up for the demonstration and is not a Graduate School policy. The business rules register ({case:business-rules}) is separate from the library; a rule can be linked to a library document.
